title: Unmet assistance among older adults coexists with food, health-cost, housing, and utility hardship
source_unit: Urban Institute December 2025 Well-Being and Basic Needs Survey published estimates

observations.period: December 2025 WBNS; older-adult and assistance-need estimates

denominator.unit: published WBNS subgroup universes; exact analytic denominators are not disclosed in the published brief

observations.method: Published cross-sectional December 2025 WBNS estimates, retaining the source's older-adult, disability, functional-limitation, assistance, and hardship subgroup definitions.
observations.uncertainty: The 2025 WBNS sample expanded to approximately 2,500 adults age 65 and older; older-adult estimates exclude institutional settings, subgroup denominators differ, and published percentages do not establish timing or causal direction.
observations.subgroup: Adults age 65 and older, older adults with disabilities, adults with functional limitations, and respondents reporting unmet assistance; subgroups are not interchangeable.
observations.counterinterpretation: Co-occurring unmet assistance and hardship may reflect disability, income, household support, housing, health needs, or other correlated exposures; the survey does not identify a service episode or assign responsibility.

related_sources.claim: WBNS survey program and design context.
WBNS study metadata and access route; direct access was restricted in the project recheck.

boundary: This is a published cross-sectional 2025 WBNS age-and-care material-security layer. It does not link a respondent to a dated service request, caregiver, agency, benefit amount, care completion, remedy, food quantity, health outcome, institutional setting, trust, political action, or recovery. The 2025 older-adult sample should not be pooled mechanically with earlier working-age WBNS estimates.
